cards.title: Should You Tell Children About Your Will?
cards.body: Family advisor Annalisa Barbieri explores whether parents should reveal inheritance plans to their children. Open communication about wills can prevent unexpected surprises that tear families apart.

cards.title: Suburban Life Revealed Hidden Family Joys
cards.body: A family's move to Melbourne suburbs initially seemed boring until they discovered community activities and local attractions. The experience showed how perspective shapes children's happiness in new environments.

cards.title: IKEA Trip Reveals Parenting Gaps
cards.body: Columnist Zoe Williams reflects on taking her son to Ikea and realizing how little domestic wisdom she's imparted. The shopping trip becomes a moment of reckoning about parenting lessons.

cards.title: Open Relationships Work With Three Young Kids
cards.body: Michael and Selena practice ethical non-monogamy while raising three children, finding it energizes their partnership. Their approach demonstrates diverse family structures can foster strong relationships.

cards.title: Maternal Ambivalence: Love, Anger, and Doubt
cards.body: Mothers simultaneously carry love, anger, joy, and doubt toward their children and motherhood. Understanding this complexity helps normalize the conflicted feelings many parents experience.

cards.title: Help Children With ADHD Flourish
cards.body: Kids with ADHD can thrive by focusing on their strengths while addressing challenges. A strengths-based approach helps build confidence and resilience.

cards.title: Teaching Children Kindness Amid Hate
cards.body: Parents can help children understand difficult emotions and resist antisemitism and hate. Teaching empathy, courage, and compassion equips kids to navigate complex social issues.

cards.title: When Your Needs Conflict With Your Child's
cards.body: Parents sometimes face situations where their needs and their child's needs don't align. It's acceptable to prioritize your own wellbeing in these difficult moments.

cards.title: Why Apologies Aren't Enough for Adult Children
cards.body: Adult children may continue referencing past parental mistakes despite receiving apologies. Understanding why requires deeper exploration of childhood impact and healing needs.
